text: The Fed is expected to hike again in December with inflation rising to 3.7%, while September payrolls badly missed at just 29,000 jobs — this stagflationary mix of rising prices and weakening employment is a real threat to stock valuations, so consider holding extra cash and being selective with new positions.

QBTS is down 59% from its high, the company is losing money, nearly a quarter of shares are sold short, and insiders are selling — this is a broken position and it's time to cut your losses and move on.

IONQ has no profits, negative free cash flow, heavy insider selling, and is down 55% from its high — the thesis here isn't working and staying in means hoping for a miracle rather than investing on evidence.
RGTI has the worst relative strength in your portfolio with shrinking revenue, no path to profitability, and heavy short interest — down 56%, this is a clear exit before it gets worse.
GOOGL is down about 14% but trades at a reasonable 21x earnings with 15% revenue growth — this pullback in one of the strongest businesses in the world is a chance to add at a better price.
Adobe at 9x earnings with 10% revenue growth and a 10% free cash flow yield looks genuinely undervalued — those are value-stock numbers on a high-quality software company.
Micron's 256% revenue growth and 4.8x PE make it one of the cheapest growth stories in your portfolio — the memory chip cycle is turning and the numbers back adding here.
PPG scores 8.1 on the breakout screener with newly positive relative strength versus the S&P 500 — this defensive industrial name breaking out could offer shelter if the economy slows further.
